about: Claims about logos-sort with their verdict and evidence. A corpus, not a request body.
verdict_field: for A/B/D/E/F rows the recorded grade; for C rows (the negative ledger) the measured RESULT

grades.MEASURED: measured end to end under the paired-A/B method
grades.INFERRED: argued from a measurement, not isolated

C. Negative ledger.verdict: the measured RESULT (every C row was implemented, measured and REJECTED)

method_note.paired_ab: two variants run adjacently on the two halves of one array, order alternated; median of the ratio with p10/p90. Drift cancels inside a pair, ordering bias across pairs.
method_note.resolving_floor: the same engine on both sides reads 1.000; 40 pairs resolve ~3.7% at 8M and ~6.1% at 1M. An effect below that is not a result.
method_note.layout_bias: engine copies differing only in renamed symbols differ up to 1.24x from code alignment, so any claim under 1.25x needs the copy assignment permuted or the mechanism traced.
method_note.verification: every benchmark checks output against a reference; ~45,899 harness property checks.
method_note.calibration_line: memcpy 64MB and std::sort 1M are printed per run; quiet is ~2.9ms/~65ms. A loaded box flatters logos, because barrier-heavy opponents lose more to preemption.

statements.section: A. Competitive position (8M f64, 20-thread single-socket box, WSL2)
statements.statement: x86-simd-sort MT beats logos 20T on every unstructured shape
statements.verdict: FALSE on AVX2 hardware after H0b + D16 (re-measured 2026-09-10)
statements.evidence: AVX-512 box, old engine: uniform 34 vs 60 ms, heavy_tail 24 vs 72, bimodal 24 vs 69, int_wide 23 vs 59. AVX2 box, new engine: logos wins uniform 26.4 vs 30.7, int_wide 25.1 vs 31.0, quantized, near_sorted, few_distinct, both block shapes; ties heavy_tail 36.7 vs 35.3; loses bimodal 41.3 vs 24.4. AVX-512 kernels are ~1.5–2× the AVX2 ones, so on AVX-512 hardware parity is plausible and unmeasured

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: The random-data 20T floor (~40 ms) is per-core scatter *latency* plus fixed cost, not bandwidth
statements.evidence: ping-pong removed 37% of traffic, time moved ~12%; write-combining is ~10%; hyperthreading gave 1.3–1.5×

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: At 20T the top-level histogram was the dominant cost, ~9× the scatter in CPU time, and it was compute (the bucket_of binary search), not memory
statements.evidence: uniform: histogram 836 thread-ms CPU vs scatter 88, leaf 313; ≤4% preempted; 49–70% of wall. After H0b the whole sort is 1.6–3× faster on those shapes

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: The 1T sequential route never runs the top-level partition (100% leaf); the 20T route pays a histogram that costs more per element than the whole 1T sort
statements.evidence: ~100 vs ~29 ns/element; explains the ~3× 20-thread speedup

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: The parallel route has a fixed cost of ~5–10 ms on this box (thread creation, barriers, P×12 buckets), so all-threads-for-any-n loses to one thread below ~5e5 elements
statements.evidence: fixed by D18; the crossover where 20 threads beat 1 is ~1M elements here

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: Noise anatomy of the reference box (make noiseprobe, 12 reps): a 1T sort is never preempted (cpu = wall) yet varies 7% median / 56% worst from sibling-hyperthread and cache contention; parallel runs lose time slices in proportion to thread count (utilisation 0.99 at 2T → 0.62 at 20T, max/min 1.4 → 2.7); best minimum at 14 threads = physical cores
statements.evidence: two hogs outside the project (VS Code software-WebGL ~44%, OneDrive ~20%) explain the session's ±12–25% bands; min-of-≥12 and interleaving are the mitigations, LOGOS_THREADS=14 for quiet numbers

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: "Bimodal" says nothing about what is inside a mode. Splitting at the gulfs is cheap and general; assuming the pieces are then uniform is not. Measured worst-mode distance from uniform: two uniform bands 0.023 (certifies), three uniform bands 0.02, two gaussians 0.30, three uneven clusters 0.32, a wide gaussian mixture does not separate into modes at all
statements.evidence: certify each piece rather than assume it; the same argument killed the exponent map, whose binades are not uniform inside either (C25)

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: Adjacency beats quiet. A machine whose speed wanders 5-10x over tens of seconds cannot be stilled, but two measurements taken back to back share its state, so the wander divides out. Pairing the variants and taking the median of 40 ratios resolves ~3.7% at 8M where best-of-N across separately compiled copies resolved ~1.25x
statements.evidence: bench_paired() in bench_common.h; alternate which half goes first, or the destination-page bias adds 2-4%

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: You cannot pin a core inside a VM. taskset in WSL2 constrains a virtual CPU number; the Windows hypervisor still places it wherever it likes. The giveaway is that a thread pinned to CPUs 12-19 ran FASTER than unpinned, when on a 6P+8E part those should be the efficiency cores
statements.verdict: MEASURED and REJECTED (FINDINGS 3u); cgroup cpuset would need root and hits the same boundary
statements.evidence: one run showed spread 1.40 -> 1.13 and the next 1.32: a single non-reproduced improvement is not a result

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A quantile splitter is a load balancer. Choosing splitters at sample quantiles equalises the buckets by construction, so the leaf phase has almost no scheduling slack left to win: traced largest-leaf-over-mean is 1.10x on uniform and 1.48x on Pareto, and the greedy makespan bound turns that into 8-11% of one phase
statements.verdict: MEASURED (make lptbench; largest-first dispatch 0.95-1.05 on seven shapes, opt-in LOGOS_LPT=1)
statements.evidence: before optimising a schedule, measure the imbalance: the bound is W/P + L(1 - 1/P), and with 12 leaves per thread a 1.1x L is worth nothing

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A runtime toggle beats a second compiled copy for an A/B. Switching a feature with getenv once per call lets one binary measure both variants, which removes the up-to-1.24x code-layout bias (B26/rule 3) instead of controlling for it
statements.verdict: MEASURED (used for lptbench; cost is one getenv against ~1 ms of serial setup per parallel sort)
statements.evidence: only works for features that are a branch, not a different code path; pair it with bench_paired

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: "Could not resolve" is not "neutral", and the difference is worth paying for. Five features carried "mixed" or "noise" verdicts reached against a ~1.25x floor. Re-run at the ~4% floor with the code-layout bias cancelled by a copy swap, all five are neutral within 0.95-1.04 across five shapes at two thread counts
statements.verdict: MEASURED (tools/ledger_rerun.py, 24 pairs x 2 orientations, 8M; the one borderline row re-checked at 80 pairs)
statements.evidence: improving the instrument tenfold IS a new angle on a closed question, and it is cheaper than another idea

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: Pairing cancels drift; only a copy swap cancels alignment. Timing two variants back to back removes the machine's thermal wander, but each variant still sits in a fixed compiled copy. Building twice with the assignment swapped gives A = E(L0/L1) and B = (1/E)(L0/L1), so sqrt(A/B) is the true effect and sqrt(A*B) is the layout bias itself
statements.verdict: MEASURED (the layout term read 0.96-1.04 over fifty cells, 0.999 on the 80-pair check)
statements.evidence: the two corrections are independent; applying only one leaves the other in the number

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A multiscale occupancy profile over (index, value) sees arrangement, and its misses fall where they cannot cost anything. With the rule fixed from six other shapes, a held-out twenty-shape zoo scored 4 of 8 arrangement shapes classified and 9 of 10 value-set shapes abstained; on the 3 cases where the engine left 1.2x or more against a sort told the structure it was blind on 0, and every miss was on a shape the engine already beats its ceiling on
statements.verdict: MEASURED (make zroute; make ztrain confirms the rule as coded matches its fitting)
statements.evidence: thin evidence, 3 opportunities; the profile names structure, it does not supply the route that uses it

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A sample cannot see order finer than its own spacing. Window-shuffled data with disorder of 2048 and latency-displaced data with disorder of 4096 read sorted or unknown to a 4096-point sample of 8M, whose spacing is 2048
statements.evidence: fine-scale order needs a linear scan; do not ask a sample for it

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A classifier's rule can be too loose while its measurement is right. The tail rule, "low early and peaks late", fired on Gray-code order, which the probe correctly saw as arranged, because consecutive codes differ by one bit
statements.evidence: fix rules on fresh shapes, never on the test set that exposed them

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: Tighten a rule on its failures, validate it on strangers. The probe's tail rule was redesigned from the two false tails a held-out zoo exposed, then scored on fifteen shapes it had never seen: false tails fell from 5 of 7 to 1 of 7 with recall unchanged at 4 of 5
statements.evidence: the survivor, a random walk, shows the limit of occupancy alone: coarse order with fine disorder looks the same whether it came from a tail or a walk

statements.section: B. Cost model (what the floor is made of)
statements.statement: A sequential route offered to a parallel sort loses, and it took two routes to make that stick. The dense-integer bitmap and then the sorted-prefix-plus-tail merge each won several times over at one thread and regressed at fourteen, the tail route to 0.34-0.87, because single-threaded passes displaced parallel routes that were already fast
statements.evidence: gate a sequential route on the sort actually running sequentially; win at P only with a parallel form of the route

statements.evidence: the leaf cost is the insertion fix-up (Devroye's n·∫f²) and the per-bucket probes, not the counters or the level count; lever is equi-depth classes gated by an ∫f² estimate, branchless fix-up, fewer probes

statements.section: C. Negative ledger (implemented, measured, rejected — do not re-run without a new angle)
statements.statement: AVX2 quicksort in the PARALLEL leaf (33k-element L2-resident buckets, make simdbench -DLOGOS_AVX2_PARALLEL)
statements.verdict: −5 to −28% at 14T, −10 to −16% at 6T on every random shape
statements.evidence: the scalar flash/coarse leaf on an L2-resident bucket is already ~9 ns/elem; the vectorized quicksort is 8.5 at 1 thread and slower under 14, on a hybrid P+E CPU (E-cores run 256-bit AVX2 double-pumped). The same code wins 1.2–1.6× sequentially, so it ships sequential-only

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: Branchless Batcher networks for 4-16 elements in the leaf, generated and proved by the 0-1 principle before being written
statements.evidence: random calls 1.03-1.06x at n=4 rising monotonically to 1.57-1.58x at n=16, two runs and both copy orientations; n=18 and 24 read 0.99 as the control; sorted rows 0.97-1.04. A small-end result, not a result at scale. SHIPPED

statements.statement: The lattice MAP phase claims chunks from an atomic counter instead of taking equal slices
statements.evidence: quantized and mod_card_30k 0.90-0.97 on 12 of 12 cells at 4M+, two runs of 60 pairs, against a null switch on the same rows at 0.97-1.04. ~1.05x. SHIPPED

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The same work queue applied to relocation's output tiles
statements.evidence: 0.96-1.04 on every cell of two runs against a prediction of 0.88-0.97. A work queue buys balance only where the CORES are the bottleneck; those phases are memcpy over disjoint ranges, bound by one memory controller. REVERTED

statements.evidence: ~1.03x, 20 of 20 cells on the winning side against a measured null. SHIPPED

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The lattice route's idle threads are its serial merge
statements.evidence: split into four profiler phases at 14 threads: map 68% at concurrency 10.72/14, merge 1.0%, emit 28% at concurrency 3.17/14, teardown 0.14%. The merge is not the problem

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The lattice route's 2ms of table teardown is worth attacking
statements.evidence: 9-14 MICROseconds, 0.14% of the route. The 2ms came from a TRACE build; a trace build gives shares, never a price against a normal build

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The lattice emit phase's low concurrency is thread imbalance
statements.evidence: every thread gets exactly n/P output positions, so it cannot be. A standalone replica splits it: create+join of 13 workers is 0.564ms of 1.597ms (35%), and the remaining fill gets only 2.7x from 14 threads because 67MB of stores at 65 GB/s is the DDR5 ceiling

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: Knowing the data FORMAT (that values are dates) beats certifying the distribution, for NUMERIC timestamps
statements.evidence: a sort TOLD the origin and step is 0.24-0.77 of the engine (1.3-4.2x slower) across six date shapes, and returns WRONG OUTPUT on day-plus-fraction, which has no exact integer form. Predicted 2-4x available

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: Knowing the date format pays when the dates are TEXT
statements.evidence: parse to a numeric key + logos_argsort_f64 + one gather is 8.48x over std::sort on std::string and 4.87x over fixed 24-byte memcmp records, 2M records, one thread. A format is worth what it saves in COMPARISON WIDTH, not in distribution knowledge

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: Projecting each element onto a sphere of radius n (x=value, y=a prime, z=the index) and sorting the projection
statements.evidence: 22.2% of 2.0M pairs at different indices come back order-INVERTED. proj_x = R*x/sqrt(x^2+p^2+z^2), and with z to 8.4M against values to 1e4 the z^2 term dwarfs x^2, so it orders by value/index. Cost alone would NOT have killed it: 2.89 ns/element against the engine's 0.60 ns addressing multiply-add

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The scale report's memory column reproduces make memprobe from an independent code path
statements.evidence: logos 15.7 bytes/element at 10M against memprobe's documented 15.5 (1.3%); the strict in-place entry and std::sort both exactly 0.0. Agreement between two independent instruments

statements.section: Measured after the truth table was last written
statements.statement: The dispatcher's frame grew across one session and that is the untraced small-call drift
statements.evidence: psort_f64 is 36,640 bytes in the committed engine and 42,576 in the working tree; stack-clash protection probes every 4096-byte page on every call, so 9 probes against 11 -- two extra on a ~17ns sorted call, which matches the recorded 1.08-1.14 drift
